address: Oudezijds Achterburgwal 233-237 / Vendelstraat 7, Amsterdam: rounded 19th-century brick building of the University of Amsterdam, with a baroque carved gateway
notes: Oudezijds Achterburgwal 233-237 (BAG: oldest part 1686, rebuilt later; roof max 22.1 m): the university building behind the Oudemanhuispoort side. Three photographed fronts. West (w02-283, 2017): a curved/rounded brick wing, four levels with a half-sunk ground floor, stone string courses, segmental brick arches over the first-floor windows and a moulded stone cornice; an iron stair leads to a side door. West (w01-282, 2025): a gabled brick house, then a baroque carved stone gateway (cartouche with crest, volutes, rusticated jambs, double leaf door with roundels) set in a lower wing with cornice. East (w03-103, 2023): brick with stone string courses, arched-brick window heads with keystone blocks and a tall arched door.

Modelled: the west (w02-283) and east (w03-103) fronts as brick-bay-grid groups (4 storeys, cornice, stone string courses). The baroque gateway (w01-282) sits on the 28 m west wall (3DBAG panel 266) whose LoD2.2 surfaces are an all-party wall (16.8 m of party height over 14.9 m eaves), so it carries no group and no entrance; it is listed in the inventory as skipped (not visible in the shell). Simplified: the segmental arch heads are flat; the rounded wing is straight (3DBAG LoD2.2 plane). Not modelled: the iron stair, lamp posts, the roof lantern and chimney. North and courtyard walls have no photograph and stay blank.

Measured 2026-10-14 (measure.ts, evidence in measured.json): groups 1 take the photo's wall and glass colour, window shape, bay count and front class; walls[1] glass #3b2a23 not used (not darker than the wall #232424 by 10 L*, or tinted): kit glass kept.
